title: WPSS/472/2014 of Shivcharan Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
WPSS No. 472 of 2014
Honíble Manoj K. Tiwari, J.
Mr. G.D. Joshi, Advocate for the
petitioner.
Mr. S.M.S. Mehta, Brief Holder for the
State of Uttarakhand/respondent nos. 1 &
2.
Mrs. Beena Pande, Standing Counsel
for the State of Uttar Pradesh/respondent
no. 3.
Heard learned counsel for the parties.
Petitioner belongs to Scheduled Caste
category, who possesses National
Apprenticeship Certificate issued by
Secretary, National Council for Vocational
Training. Petitioner responded to
Advertisement No. 1/104/2010 issued by
Director, Training & Employment,
Uttarakhand, whereby applications were
invited for the post of Instructor (Welder).
According to the petitioner, by virtue of his
score of marks in the selection, his name
figured in the list of successful candidates,
however, appointment was withheld from
him only on the ground that he does not
possess National Trade Certificate issued by
National Council for Vocational Training.
Learned counsel for the petitioner
refers to the said advertisement and submits
that, as per the advertisement, a candidate
was required either to have National Trade
Certificate or National Apprenticeship
Certificate and there was nothing in the
advertisement to show that a candidate is
required to have both these Certificates. He
further submits that since petitioner had
submitted National Apprenticeship
Certificate alongwith his application,
therefore, there was no reason to withhold
appointment from him.

Per contra, learned Brief Holder for the
State of Uttarakhand submits that the
Industrial Training Institute, from where
petitioner got training, is not affiliated to
National Council for Vocational Training. He
further submits that since there was a doubt
regarding validity of the National
Apprenticeship Certificate possessed by the
petitioner, therefore, respondent no. 2 sent a
letter on 28.04.2014 to the Director General
of Employment & Training, New Delhi
seeking guidance, however he submits, that
no reply has been received in response to the
said letter.
Learned counsel for the petitioner
submits that, pursuant to petitionerís
application made under Right to Information
Act, petitioner has been informed by Joint
Director, Regional Directorate of
Apprenticeship Training, Kanpur that
National Apprenticeship Certificate
possessed by the petitioner is valid in terms
of Apprenticeship Act, 1961. Thus, learned
counsel for the petitioner submits that there
is no reason to doubt petitionerís eligibility
for appointment. He submits that one post of
Instructor (Welder) reserved for Scheduled
Caste category person is still lying vacant.
Having regard to the facts and
circumstances of the case, this Court thinks
that interest of justice would be served, if
petitioner is permitted to make a
representation regarding his appointment
against available vacancy, to Director,
Training & Employment, Uttarakhand, who
shall take appropriate decision thereupon, in
accordance with law, within stipulated time
frame.
Accordingly, writ petition is disposed of
with liberty to the petitioner to make a
representation regarding his appointment

against available vacancy within two weeks
from today. If such a representation is made,
the Director, Training & Employment,
Uttarakhand shall examine petitionerís claim
and pass appropriate order, in accordance
with law, within a period of eight weeks from
the date of receipt of such representation
along with certified copy of this order.
 (Manoj K. Tiwari, J.)
Arpan 25.04.2019
